reading.h2: What Is the Sacrament of Matrimony?

reading.p: The Sacrament of Matrimony is the holy service through which the bridegroom and the bride are united and granted divine grace. This grace sanctifies their matrimonial union, making it perfect and spiritual, like the unity of Christ and the Church.

reading.h2: Institution of the Sacrament in the Old Testament

reading.quote: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.

reading.p: Marriage was instituted by God from the very beginning of human creation. Adam and Eve were united as husband and wife, and God Himself blessed this union. This shows that marriage was always meant to be a divine institution.

reading.h2: Institution of the Sacrament in the New Testament

reading.p: In His teaching in Matthew 19, Christ is not introducing a brand-new teaching but restoring and elevating the original meaning of marriage that God intended from the beginning. The Pharisees were testing Him about divorce, and Christ pointed them back to Genesis, emphasizing that marriage was not meant to be broken.

In the Jewish context, marriage was often seen more in terms of family, children, and inheritance, rather than explicitly as a mystical union of two becoming one flesh. Christ revealed the spiritual depth of marriage: it is not just a social contract or family arrangement, but a sacramental mystery where two truly become one in God.

reading.quote: And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

reading.p: The Church teaches three divine goals of marriage, each grounded in Scripture.

reading.quote: Male and female He created them. And God blessed them, and said, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

reading.h3: 2. Mutual Help Between Husband and Wife

reading.quote: It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a help meet for him.
To avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband... for it is better to marry than to burn.

reading.p: In Orthodox theology, every Sacrament, or Mystery, has two parts. The first is an outward, visible sign, something we can see, hear, or touch, such as words, actions, or physical elements like oil, bread, wine, or water. The second is an inward, invisible grace, which is the divine reality given by God through the Holy Spirit. The outward sign is the visible action or symbol that expresses and communicates the hidden grace of God.
In the Sacrament of Matrimony the outward signs include:

list: The sacramental act the priest performs

reading.p: The inward grace of Matrimony accomplishes what no outward action could do on its own:

list: To sanctify the matrimonial union and make it a spiritual one.
To help the husband and wife keep themselves united and unseparated, just as the unity of Christ with the Church is everlasting.
To keep the husband and wife loyal and faithful to each other.

reading.h2: Obligations of Wife and Husband Before Marriage

reading.p: The grace of Christ is given only within the Church. The sacraments, including Matrimony, cannot be bestowed upon non-Christians.

reading.h3: 2. Both must belong to the Orthodox Church

reading.p: Because the Sacrament of Matrimony is received within the Church, if one is not Orthodox, he or she must first be united to the Church before receiving this Mystery.

reading.h3: 3. The couple must not be bound by forbidden kinship

reading.p: Carnal kinship (blood relation) or spiritual affinity, such as godparent relationships, creates an impediment to marriage.

reading.h3: 4. Both must freely consent to the marriage

reading.p: The sacrament requires the free will of the bride and groom. Parental desire alone is not enough. The priest must ask each of them, privately and publicly, to confirm their agreement.

reading.h2: Marriage: At and After the Sacrament

reading.p: Because Matrimony is a sacrament, it must be performed in the Church and not outside of it. Priests must teach the faithful this truth.

list: Faithfulness and Unity: husband and wife are joined as one flesh (Matthew 19:4-5).
Marriage until death: if a spouse dies, the other may remarry, but 'only in the Lord' (1 Corinthians 7:39).
Indissolubility: there is to be no separation except for fornication (Matthew 19:6, 9).

studyGuide.overview: Holy Matrimony is the sacrament through which a bride and bridegroom are united and granted divine grace that sanctifies their union, making it like the unity of Christ and the Church. Instituted by God at creation and restored and elevated by Christ in Matthew 19, it is not a mere contract but a sacramental Mystery with outward signs, inward grace, conditions for the couple, and lifelong obligations of faithfulness, unity, and indissolubility.
keyPoints: Matrimony is a Sacrament (Mystery) that unites the couple and grants sanctifying grace like the unity of Christ and the Church.
Marriage was instituted by God at creation (Genesis 1:27-28) and restored and elevated by Christ (Matthew 19:4-6).
Its three divine goals are the growth of mankind, mutual help between spouses, and a guard against carnal temptation.
Like every Mystery, it has an outward visible sign (declaration, the priest's act, anointing with oil) and an inward invisible grace.
Before marriage, both must be Christians and Orthodox, free of forbidden kinship, and must freely consent.
It must be performed in the Church; after marriage it calls for faithfulness, unity, marriage until death, and indissolubility except for fornication.
reviewQuestions: How does the lesson define the Sacrament of Matrimony?
How was marriage instituted in the Old Testament, and how did Christ restore and elevate it in the New?
What are the three divine goals of matrimony, and what Scripture supports each?
What is the difference between the outward sign and the inward grace of a Sacrament, and what are the outward signs of Matrimony?
What are the four obligations a couple must meet before marriage, and why does each matter?
What does the Church teach about where marriage must be performed and about its indissolubility?

checks: Matrimony is presented as a true Sacrament/Mystery conferring sanctifying grace, consistent with Tewahedo sacramental theology.
The union is likened to the everlasting unity of Christ and the Church, an image faithful to the tradition.
The sacramental structure of outward sign and inward grace through the Holy Spirit is correctly stated.

Conditions (both Christian and Orthodox, free of forbidden kinship, free consent) and obligations (in-Church celebration, faithfulness, indissolubility except for fornication, remarriage only in the Lord) match Orthodox canonical teaching.
